findings.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — P1: `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` makes a thumbnail-rendering setting select the original-upload transform, so disabling animated thumbnails silently persists a first-frame-only GIF instead of the user’s animated source.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65 — P2: `attempt = 5` makes reduction a fixed-effort loop rather than an output-size invariant, so a tempfile still above `max_image_size_kb` after five passes is handed to the upload boundary as though automatic downsize had completed.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — P2: `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the preceding width/height `downsize` definition in Ruby, silently changing the helper’s established public shape from separate dimensions to ImageMagick syntax and leaving existing callers without a compatibility boundary.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024;` rejects an 11 MB image in the browser before the new server-side downsize loop can run, so images above 10 MB are never automatically reduced.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, "discourse-upload-#{type}")` prevents API URL uploads larger than 10 MB from reaching the downsize loop, leaving that upload path unable to fulfill automatic reduction for those images.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a fixed limit stops `max_attachment_size_kb` from propagating to attachment validation, so configured attachment limits above or below 10 MB are no longer enforced client-side.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024;` makes every 413 error claim a 10 MB limit even when `max_image_size_kb` (or the failing attachment limit) is configured differently, so the upload error no longer reports the setting that rejected the upload.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` routes enabled animated GIFs to `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`, but that option requires a `widthxheight` rectangle, so the command fails and oversized animated GIFs are never reduced.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` replaces the per-type site setting, so an instance configured to allow images or attachments larger than 10 MB now rejects those uploads in the browser before the server can process them.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Replacing the type-specific site setting with a 10 MB cap makes image uploads above 10 MB fail client validation even when an administrator configured a larger allowable image size, so those configured-large images are not automatically downsized.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — P1 (confidence: 99): `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces rather than overloads the existing five-argument method, so any caller using `downsize(from, to, width, height, opts)` now raises `ArgumentError` and its image-processing job fails.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — P1: An API caller can set `type` to `image; <command> #`, which becomes part of the `FileHelper.download` tempfile path and is interpolated unquoted by `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` into the shell command, yielding remote command execution as the application user when the downloaded URL names an image.

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — P1: `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` makes a thumbnail-rendering setting select the original-upload transform, so disabling animated thumbnails silently persists a first-frame-only GIF instead of the user’s animated source.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at line 67 that `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is passed to `OptimizedImage.downsize()`. This setting controls whether thumbnails should be animated, but here it's being used to control whether the original uploaded image preserves animation during the downsize loop. If `allow_animated_thumbnails` is false (user doesn't want animated thumbnails), the original GIF upload would be converted to a static first-frame image, which is incorrect behavior - the original should preserve animation regardless of thumbnail settings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65 — P2: `attempt = 5` makes reduction a fixed-effort loop rather than an output-size invariant, so a tempfile still above `max_image_size_kb` after five passes is handed to the upload boundary as though automatic downsize had completed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a loop that attempts to downsize an image up to 5 times (attempt = 5, decrementing each iteration). After the loop completes, the code proceeds to Upload.create_for() regardless of whether the tempfile size is still above max_image_size_kb. There's no check after the loop to verify the file was successfully reduced to the allowed size, meaning oversized files could be uploaded if 5 iterations weren't sufficient to reduce them below the limit.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a logical inconsistency. The diff shows that FileHelper.download is hardcoded to 10.megabytes limit (line 55), but the downsize loop (lines 63-68) only runs when tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. If max_image_size_kb is set to something larger than 10MB (10*1024 KB), images between 10MB and max_image_size_kb uploaded via API URL would fail at the download step before reaching the downsize loop. This is a real logical defect where the hardcoded 10MB download limit prevents larger images from being automatically downsized when the site setting allows larger uploads.

This hardcoded value is used in the error message `I18n.t('post.errors.file_too_large', { max_size_kb: maxSizeKB })`. This is a real bug where the user-facing error message is misleading.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` replaces the per-type site setting, so an instance configured to allow images or attachments larger than 10 MB now rejects those uploads in the browser before the server can process them.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows that line 182 changes from `var maxSizeKB = Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` (which reads the per-type site setting) to `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` (a hardcoded 10MB value). This means if an instance has configured max_image_size_kb or max_attachment_size_kb to be greater than 10MB (10240KB), the client-side validation will now incorrectly reject uploads that the server would accept. This is a real behavioral regression for instances with larger upload limits.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Replacing the type-specific site setting with a 10 MB cap makes image uploads above 10 MB fail client validation even when an administrator configured a larger allowable image size, so those configured-large images are not automatically downsized.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in utilities.js line 182, the code changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB). This means the client-side validation now uses a fixed 10MB limit regardless of what administrators configure in SiteSettings. If an admin configures a larger limit (e.g., 20MB), the client will reject files over 10MB before they even reach the server where the automatic downsizing logic (added in uploads_controller.rb) could process them. This is a real defect where the hardcoded client-side limit prevents the server-side auto-downsize feature from working for images between 10MB and the configured max size.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — P1 (confidence: 99): `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces rather than overloads the existing five-argument method, so any caller using `downsize(from, to, width, height, opts)` now raises `ArgumentError` and its image-processing job fails.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that the original `downsize` method with signature `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (5 arguments) is being replaced by a new method `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (4 arguments). Lines 142-143 show the old method being modified to call optimize with dimensions string, and then lines 145-147 show a completely new method definition with the same name but different arity. This means any existing callers using the 5-argument signature `downsize(from, to, width, height, opts)` will fail with ArgumentError because Ruby will use the 4-argument method definition. The finding correctly identifies this as a breaking change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — P2 (confidence: 99): `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` replaces the per-site upload limit for both images and attachments, so a site configured to allow more than 10 MB now blocks otherwise valid user uploads in the browser before sending a request.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows that line 182 changes from `var maxSizeKB = Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` (which reads the per-site configured limit) to `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` (a hardcoded 10MB limit). This means sites that have configured upload limits higher than 10MB will now have their users blocked from uploading files that were previously allowed, as the client-side validation will reject them before they reach the server. This is a real behavioral regression for sites with higher configured limits.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10MB` replaces the type-specific limit for both images and attachments, so the image-downsizing feature also changes which oversized non-image attachments the client permits.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that line 182 changes from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` (which would use type-specific settings like max_image_size_kb or max_attachment_size_kb) to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB) for all file types. This means non-image attachments will now be allowed up to 10MB on the client side regardless of the actual server-side attachment size limit. The server-side downsizing logic (in uploads_controller.rb) only applies to images (`FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`), so oversized non-image attachments that pass client validation will fail on the server. This is a real behavioral change that could cause user confusion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — P1: An API caller can set `type` to `image; <command> #`, which becomes part of the `FileHelper.download` tempfile path and is interpolated unquoted by `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` into the shell command, yielding remote command execution as the application user when the downloaded URL names an image.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that the `type` parameter becomes part of the tempfile path and is interpolated into shell commands. However, looking at the diff, the tempfile path comes from `tempfile.path` which is the path of a Ruby Tempfile object created by `FileHelper.download`. The `type` parameter is only used in the tempfile naming pattern `discourse-upload-#{type}` passed to FileHelper.download, but this is just a prefix for the tempfile name, not directly interpolated into shell commands. The `OptimizedImage.downsize` call uses `tempfile.path` which is a system-generated temporary file path, not user-controlled. The finding misreads how the code works - the type parameter doesn't flow into the shell command execution in the way described.
